decisions.title: A very brief possession
decisions.situation: A soap bubble floats past your nose. You reach for it. Your new favourite thing has already resigned.

choices.label: Go after the next one
Watch where it goes
Complain about the disappearing bubble

result.title: Plenty of vacancies
result.body: There are more bubbles. You spend several happy minutes failing to keep any of them.

journal.text: I chased soap bubbles and caught absolutely nothing.

decisions.title: Building regulations
decisions.situation: You stack three blocks. For a moment, the tower stands. Then you discover what your elbow has been planning.

choices.label: Build it again with a wider bottom
Knock down the next tower on purpose
Line the blocks up on the floor

result.title: A better foundation
result.body: The new tower survives your elbow. Your hand brings it down a little later.

journal.text: I rebuilt a block tower with a wider base.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Miguel asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Show Miguel your disappearing treasure
Try the other sock
Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Miguel supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Miguel the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour
Send the same letter again

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: The watermelon investigation
decisions.situation: Miguel jokes that swallowing a seed could grow a watermelon in your tummy. You have questions. Several concern the size of your tummy.

choices.label: Demand to know where the leaves go
Draw a plan for your indoor garden
Announce you are growing a fruit salad

result.title: The witness changes their story
result.body: Miguel admits it was a joke and explains what seeds actually need. You ask why they left out the soil problem.

journal.text: I questioned Miguel until they explained a joke about swallowing seeds.

decisions.title: Missing person: teddy’s eye
decisions.situation: One of your old teddy’s button eyes comes off. You ask Miguel whether teddy needs an ambulance.

choices.label: Help with a supervised repair
Give teddy a pirate patch
Stay with teddy until it is fixed

result.title: Outpatient care
result.body: Miguel handles the needle. You choose where the eye belongs.

journal.text: I helped Miguel repair my teddy.

decisions.title: The bean is not thriving
decisions.situation: The class bean plant is dead. Laura asks why your progress chart still says “thriving”. You added a smiley face this morning.

choices.label: Write an honest report on its demise
Ask Laura where you went wrong
Give it an emotional farewell speech

result.title: A useful post-mortem
result.body: You record the dry soil and brown leaves. Laura gives credit for the observations, rather than your earlier optimism.

journal.text: I corrected my report about a dead classroom bean plant.

decisions.title: Your name on the cover
decisions.situation: Alice asks you to share a class project. Laura has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.

choices.label: Promise to write your section
Ask to work separately
Admit you cannot commit

result.title: Future You has been notified
result.body: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

journal.text: I agreed to write a section of a class project with Alice.

decisions.title: The project is due
decisions.situation: Alice is putting the class project together. Laura wants your section today. The blank page has enjoyed two months of peace.

choices.label: Finish your section
Ask Laura for help
Leave your section blank

result.title: Your name belongs on it
result.body: You finish your section and explain it to Alice. Laura records the work you actually did.

journal.text: I finished my section of the class project with Alice.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: A promise remembered
decisions.situation: Two years after that class project, Alice Souza brings it up. Back then, you finished your section.

choices.label: Remember doing your part
Tell Alice it does not matter
Leave it in the past

result.title: An old project, an honest conversation
result.body: You acknowledge that you finished your section. Alice hears you out.

journal.text: I talked honestly with Alice about our old project, when I finished my section.

decisions.title: Little Star, big photograph
decisions.situation: Your school-photo proof arrives. You wore an old top that barely fits. Across your chest, in extremely clear letters, it says “LITTLE STAR”.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
Sign the proof like a celebrity
Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits

result.title: Now a very large head
result.body: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.

journal.text: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

decisions.title: A complaint from past you
decisions.situation: You find a childhood letter addressed to yourself. It says, “If you are not a dinosaur by thirteen, you have ruined everything.” There is a drawing of the expected dinosaur.

choices.label: Make a tail out of socks and deliver a roar
Write a formal rejection on the back
Destroy the evidence

result.title: Partial compliance
result.body: The tail falls off during your first turn. You add “technical difficulties” beneath the original demand and draw yourself with better knees.

journal.text: I answered a childhood demand to become a dinosaur by making a sock tail.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Miguel one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Stop before they can demonstrate
Agree on one round each, then stop
Demand rematches until you win

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Miguel seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Miguel I would.

decisions.title: That is definitely your voice
decisions.situation: Miguel sends a voice note pretending to be you: “I would love to do all the washing-up forever.” Their impression makes you sound like a distressed goose.

choices.label: Request a less insulting goose
Offer one actual round of washing-up
Send an impression of them volunteering instead

result.title: A second audition
result.body: Miguel sends a deeper version. Now you sound like a goose with a cold. You both give up trying to discuss the dishes.

journal.text: I demanded a better impression after Miguel impersonated me in a voice note.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs R$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Brasília takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Brasília unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Brasília.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Brasília, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Brasília.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

Build a grand explanation around the pose

Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

Watch the demonstrations first
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.
I was born on 29 February 2024 in Brasília, Brazil.
My name is Helena Santos. I’m a girl.
My mother is Miguel Santos, 24. She works as a barista.
At home, it’s just my mother and me.
